editorial.summary: A second Big Bear recording opens with Steve Lee freestyling over Money Mark's music, then returns to the Lee brothers' running comparison. The first sustained discussion revisits Bobby Lee and Kalilah's Tinder origin. Kalilah says Bobby deleted Tinder during her hospitalization but later reinstalled it, accumulated matches and was discovered using it in Vancouver. Bobby says he restored it in Houston to demonstrate the app and forgot to remove it. The room distinguishes curiosity and fantasy from cheating, while also naming matches, swiping, a reported shoulder check and a recurring habit of defending Bobby. Kalilah then counters idealized relationship advice with the domestic reality of a five-year balcony urine container. The title comes from her description of Bobby's brief burst of rapid sex followed by a forehead kiss. That opens a long, explicit but presented-as-consensual discussion of sexual noises, awkwardness, death/humiliation play and intricate fantasy. The record preserves this material without treating statements inside roleplay as admissions. It separately flags adult age-regression, incest, death and minor-coded fantasies, and it corrects but does not endorse the room's loose clinical terminology. A discussion of Elliot Rodger and Seung-Hui Cho mixes public mass killings, racial slurs, stereotypes, anti-bullying fear and David's counterfactual claim that another life path could have led him toward Columbine-like violence; the room explicitly says murder is wrong, and the record does not convert the counterfactual into a present threat. Episode 134's forced genital-touch event is recalled and remains classified as nonconsensual. The group then reveals shared access to Critter's social accounts, discovers a Tinder impersonator using his photos, and creates a collective profile. Those facts are retained while private operators, matches, workers and discoverability mechanics are restricted. The masturbation challenge, Macau proposal, strip-club stories, Asa Akira's book tour, sibling support and pressure on Bobby and Kalilah to stay overnight all continue prior threads. Near the end, the cast proposes replacement racial and homophobic code words. The source speech and its premise remain uncensored, but the invented labels are documented as an episode-specific racist-comedy bit rather than adopted as archival categories. The formal ending is followed by a music session; decoder loops at the opening and during the jam are marked indistinct instead of rendered as dialogue. No named line-level transcript is published because held-out speaker validation remains insufficient.
